title: Next Iteration Initialization Run
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}:\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$ be an oracle, let $x$ be a finite Boolean string, let $S$ be a machine state, and let $M:\mathbb{Z}\to\{0,1\}$ be a memory function. Suppose every register value in $S$ is at most $B$ and $S.s+1\le B$. Starting in the next-iteration initialization state with registers $S$, memory $M$, and memory head at $0$, the machine reaches a configuration in the first-search copy phase with radius $S.s+1$, registers $U,V,w,K,B_s,c,c_1,s_1$ all zero, memory $M$, and head at $0$; at every earlier configuration, all register values are at most $B$, the memory head lies between $0$ and $P$, and the current instruction satisfies the machine's register-comparison side condition.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{orc}$ maps one of four indices and a Boolean string to a Boolean
$S$ is a machine state whose register values are all at most $B$
$M$ is an integer-indexed Boolean memory function
replaced:
Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean oracle indexed by four
possibilities, let $x$ be a Boolean string, let $S$ be a register state, and let $M$ be
a Boolean-valued memory on the integers. Assume every register value in $S$ is at most
$B$, and that $S.s+1\le B$. Starting with the machine in the next-iteration
initialization state, register values $S$, memory $M$, and head position $0$, it reaches
the first copy instruction of the next first search with the radius increased by one,
registers $U,V,w,K,B_s,c,c_1,s_1$ set to zero, and memory and head position still $M$
and $0$; every configuration before that reached configuration satisfies the guard
$G(x,B,P)$.
